I will keep my plan practical and familiar to Quzhou County conditions. I am in the North China Plain, so my main system will still be winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that rotation fits my climate, my irrigation habits, and my need for stable grain output. At 68, I do not want a crop mix that is too scattered or too labor-intensive, so I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize double-cropping system and set aside a smaller piece for spring peanuts to spread risk, improve cash flow, and ease pressure on soil-borne problems from continuous grain planting. Because I am well educated, I will not farm by habit alone; I will control fertilizer rates more carefully, avoid excessive nitrogen, irrigate at the key growth stages instead of watering blindly, and spray only when field scouting shows real pressure. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly raises yield stability. For tillage, I will mainly use rotary tillage because it balances residue handling, seedbed quality, and labor efficiency for me. My goal is steady output, manageable fieldwork, and lower waste rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
